note: M8 head-to-head. llama.cpp run on the SAME NVFP4 weights: convert_hf_to_gguf.py preserved the checkpoint's nvfp4 tensors, so the GGUF is 26.28 GiB of nvfp4 and this is a like-for-like comparison, not a different quantization.

llamacpp.commit: fix(mamba): make time-step projection input contiguous (#28832)

gb10_engine.note: prefill is one 64-wide tile pass, so t<=64 costs one weight pass; the 512-token projection is 8 such passes.

verdict.ttft: LOSE: 434 ms for 59 prompt tokens vs 640.9 ms for 512 in llama.cpp. Compare rates, not totals: this engine prefills at 7.36 ms/token against llama.cpp's 1.25 ms/token, an ~5.9x deficit. The totals are not comparable because the prompt lengths differ.
verdict.batch: WIN: 47.78 tok/s at 16 sequences in the engine; 19.83 tok/s delivered through the endpoint.

staleness_note: The gb10_engine block previously held round-27 numbers (ttft 6273 ms, i.e. prefill one token at a time). Corrected to measured values; re-measure rather than trust any figure here.
